item.title: Casey Viera returns to San Antonio's KENS 5 as sports anchor after a year away
item.description: Sports anchor Casey Viera has returned to KENS 5 in San Antonio after a little over a year since leaving the station. (Courtesy of Casey Viera) San Antonio viewers are about to see a new face on their TV screens. But one station's new addition is a face you may have seen before. Casey Viera, who spent about three and a half years with local CBS affiliate KENS 5 , announced on social media on Thursday, October 29, that he'll be making a comeback in San Antonio. "Happy to share I've returned back to @KENS5 as a Sports Anchor," Viera wrote in a post on X . "Thrilled to be back to make more memories in such an exciting time in San Antonio with a place that's given me some of the best times of my career." According to LinkedIn, Viera was with KENS 5 from January 2022 until May 2025, where viewers saw anchored the 6 and 10 p.m. sportscasts. Viera told MySA his contract with the station timed out amid TEGNA's merger with Nexstar Media Group , though he never wanted to leave because it's the "best newsroom I've ever worked in." "It was a place that I felt like when I started there, I just gelled immediately. And it's the type of thing, when you're in this field, that doesn't come about a whole lot," Viera said. The exterior of the KENS5 newsroom. (Frankie Cardenas/MySA) He never left San Antonio, though. With a young son who's now almost three, and with his wife's roots in Floresville, Viera said he "wasn't going anywhere." After leaving KENS 5, the Hofstra University grad stayed in sports as the play-by-play voice for St. Mary's University and Our Lady of the Lake University athletics. Since October 2025, he's hosted the Locked On Spurs postgame show and S purs Squad Show . Staying here kept the door open with KENS 5 - a new chapter he said he's "happy" and "grateful" to step into. He's most excited to keep connecting with "passionate" Spurs fans in San Antonio and to provide locals "some moment of levity" through sports. Because Locked On is also a TEGNA property, he'll be able to continue the show as well. "Most people don't get the opportunity that I get that I've received with this once, let alone twice," he said. "I just want people to know that the magnitude of the job, whatever it may be, doesn't get beyond me. I enjoy what I do." item.title: Jalen Brunson pays tribute to Bulls analyst Stacey King: ‘We miss him’
item.description: Credit: CSN, MSG The defending NBA champion New York Knicks defeated the Chicago Bulls at the United Center on Wednesday night, but after the game, the focus was on remembering someone who couldn’t be there. Jalen Brunson scored 38 points and dished 7 assists in 35 minutes, helping the Knicks improve to 2-3. Afterward, he took some time to share some kind words about Stacey King, the Bulls broadcaster who died from hypertensive cardiovascular disease in June at the age of 59. “Can I say one thing? I just wanted to say R.I.P., Stacey King, who we lost recently,” Brunson said after the Knicks’ win. “A person I knew when I was in high school out here. He supported our team, his kids went to Stevenson. Just to see him not here, it’s a little sad. So I just wanna say, my thoughts and prayers are with him and his family. We miss him.” “Can I say one thing? RIP Stacey King who we lost recently. A person I knew when I was in high school here. He supported our team…his kids went to Stevenson. Just to see him not here today…My thoughts & prayers are with him & his family. We miss him” – Jalen Brunson in Chicago https://t.co/6gsWj3idC6 — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 29, 2026 As Brunson mentioned, he played for Adelai E. Stevenson High School in Lincolnshire, Ill., graduating in 2015. King’s children attended the school, and he was known as an ardent supporter of the basketball program, which won the Class 4A state title in 2015. King won three NBA championships with the Bulls alongside Michael Jordan in the ’90s and later became the team’s beloved color commentator for nearly 20 years. Fans highly regarded King for his memorable, energetic calls , penchant for nicknames, and ability to meet the moment during broadcasts . Adam Amin and King regularly ranked among the best in Awful Announcing’s reader polls , most recently as the third-best local broadcast team in the NBA. Amin paid tribute to King during the Bulls’ season opener , saying, “We love you very much, Stacey. And we appreciate everything you did for us, everything you did with us.” The Bulls are filling the seat next to Amin with a rotating cast of analysts , including Kendall Gill, Robbie Hummel, Will Perdue, Bill Wennington, and Scott Williams. item.title: Brewers Manager Pat Murphy Calls Yankees a ‘Horseshit Team’ Moments After Winning World Series
item.description: Image Credit: By Fotopersbureau De Boer - HDL.Handle.net - CC0/ Wikimedia Commons. Pat Murphy had just won the World Series when Jake Bauers approached him with a baseball. The Milwaukee Brewers first baseman was carrying the ball from the final out of Game 5. Murphy gave him a hug, then unexpectedly turned the conversation toward the New York Yankees. The Brewers manager, 67, used “horseshit” to describe Bauers' former club during an exchange captured by Spectrum News 1 Wisconsin. The camera was recording Milwaukee's on-field celebration when the conversation took its detour through the Bronx. Milwaukee had defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 at Tropicana Field on October 28, winning the series in five games and claiming the franchise's first championship. The Brewers had last reached the Fall Classic in 1982, when they lost to the St. Louis Cardinals. For Bauers, 31, the celebration arrived with another career decision approaching. He is entering free agency after playing on a one-year, $2.7 million contract, and Murphy expects him to command a much bigger payday. Bauers Tells Murphy He Won't Be Easy to Get Rid Of Murphy accused Yankees players of looking out for themselves and urged Bauers to remember how Milwaukee had done things. Bauers answered with a joke about staying put. According to UPI , he told Murphy, “you ain't getting rid of me that easy.” The two shared a laugh during the exchange. The clubs also spent very different amounts on their rosters. The Big Lead reported a payroll of approximately $146 million for Milwaukee, compared with more than $300 million for New York. Bauers Hit Career Highs After Struggling in His Yankees Season Bauers hit .202 with 12 home runs in 84 games for New York in 2023. That November, the Yankees traded him to Milwaukee for minor league outfielders Jace Avina and Brian Sánchez. The improvement took time. He batted .199 in his first Brewers season and .235 in 2025 before raising that average to .266 this year. His 26 home runs and 86 RBIs were career highs, as were his 127 hits and 144 games played. MLB lists his regular-season OPS at .873. He then earned National League Championship Series MVP honors as Milwaukee swept the Los Angeles Dodgers. His NLCS included a 12-pitch walk against Yoshinobu Yamamoto and an 11-pitch home run off Blake Snell. Bauers drove in six runs during that series, but his bat cooled in the World Series, when he went 2 for 21. Across the entire postseason, he hit .191 with one home run. item.title: F1’s Gulf Finale Doesn’t Hinge on a UK Travel Notice. It Hinges on Freight.
item.description: Lando Norris at Suzuka in March 2026. Photo: Martin Lee / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) The tidy version of this story says a UK travel notice has put the last two Formula 1 races of 2026 in doubt. The primary documents say something messier, and more useful: the paragraph in Whitehall isn’t what moves a Grand Prix. Freight, airspace and the calendar’s shrinking list of escape routes are. What the UK actually changed The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office updated its Qatar and United Arab Emirates pages on 27 October. The only listed change is “updated information about regional tensions.” The warning text calls the Middle East context “deeply unpredictable,” says the risk of sudden escalation is high, and tells travellers to prepare for flight cancellations, airspace closures and disruption. What neither page carries, as of Thursday, is an advise-against-all-but-essential-travel headline. That matters because it separates two things people keep welding together: a government telling its citizens to stay home, and a sanctioning body deciding it cannot run an event. Nobody has announced the second. I could not find an FIA or Formula 1 statement changing either round, and F1’s own Qatar race page still lists the weekend for 27 to 29 November, with Abu Dhabi to follow on 4 to 6 December. My read, and it is a read: the update is a signal to watch, not a verdict. What would turn it into a verdict is already on the public record this year. The precedent that matters is the one with a paper trail In March the FIA said the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix would not take place in April , citing “the ongoing situation in the Middle East region.” In July the FIA and F1 confirmed Malaysia would host the Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang on 2 to 4 October. Then came the one I think is the best guide. When the FIA and the World Endurance Championship scrapped their Qatar and Bahrain rounds on 28 July, the stated driver was “ongoing regional developments affecting freight and travel arrangements.” Not a travel advisory. Logistics. Barcelona and Monza took the dates, and the WEC’s organisers said they were committed to returning to both Gulf venues in 2027. We covered what that meant on the grid in our look at Qatar keeping its name on the WEC entry list and how the substitute Barcelona round could swing the titles . Max Verstappen in Red Bull practice running at the 2025 Italian Grand Prix, shown as an archive image. Image credit: Eustace Bagg / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0) Why the lead time is the real story Here is the awkward implication. The Sepang switch was announced roughly ten weeks before its scheduled date, and the WEC’s July call came more than two months before Barcelona. Qatar is about four weeks out. Whatever the FCDO page says, the window in which a series can swap a venue without wrecking freight bookings, hotel blocks and promoter contracts is closing fast. The paddock has noticed. item.title: Canelo and Mbilli have their final say in Riyadh as fight week moves ahead
item.description: Canelo Alvarez, left, and WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli pose during Thursday’s final press conference in Riyadh. The two fight Saturday at Kingdom Arena. RIYADH — Canelo Alvarez turned professional on Oct. 29, 2005. Exactly 21 years later, he sat on stage at the final press conference for his WBC super middleweight title fight against Christian Mbilli and made it clear he still sees himself as a man chasing something. “I’m the challenger now,” Alvarez said. “But guess what? Always in my mind, I’m the champion since I was a little kid.” Alvarez (63-3-2, 39 KOs) and Mbilli (29-0-1, 24 KOs) meet Saturday at Kingdom Arena, with the main event on DAZN pay-per-view. The card is billed as Mexico vs. the World, but when Canelo Promotions CEO Richard Schaefer introduced Alvarez’s trainer, he said some people are calling it Eddie Reynoso vs. the World, since Reynoso has eight fighters on the bill. Reynoso, who has been in Alvarez’s corner for more than 20 years, took the joke and turned it into a tribute. Speaking in Spanish, with a translator relaying his words, he noted that Alvarez was reaching his 21st year as a pro and said he could not be prouder. “Everyone says, ‘Yeah, it’s me against the world,’ but it’s really him who steps up into the ring,” Reynoso said through the translator. He called Alvarez the most successful Mexican boxer in the history of the sport, said Saturday will show who has been the best in the history of Mexico, and said they are going after the WBC title, the first one they won together. The French-born, Montreal-based Mbilli, a 2016 Olympian, is the reigning, undefeated WBC champion, and Thursday was his last chance to speak to the room before the weigh-in on Friday. He kept it short. He thanked his team, said he respects Alvarez’s career, and then made his pitch. “I’m ready to shock the world,” Mbilli said. “On Saturday will be a different story, and I’m coming for the win.” When the moderator asked how he plans to knock out a man who has never touched the canvas in more than 500 professional rounds, Mbilli gave nothing away. “We’re going to see,” he said. “That’s why you don’t want to miss the fight.” He added that his camp was the best of his career and that he does not need anything extra to win, only to be himself. item.title: 📹 Pedro and Lino shine, Flamengo thrash Vasco and stay clear at the top
item.description: 📹 Pedro and Lino shine, Flamengo thrash Vasco and stay clear at the top At the Estádio Nilton Santos, Flamengo thrashed Vasco 4–1 on Thursday (29) in Matchday 33 of the 2026 Brasileirão. The Red and Blacks have not lost to their rivals in the national league since 2015! Despite the historic rivalry between the clubs, the gap in quality between their current squads once again proved decisive in the derby. Just 10 minutes into the game, Pedro popped up in the box to head home Varela's cross from the right. The No. 9 had not scored for Flamengo since September 20, in a 2–1 win over RB Bragantino. Vasco were not rattled by falling behind and quickly equalized. Brenner received the ball on the left side of the box and cut it back for Lescano to level the score. Still in the first half, Pedro popped up in the box again like a true center-forward, pouncing on a rebound from goalkeeper Léo Jardim to put Flamengo back in front. It was the Flamengo striker's 28th goal of the season! After the break, it did not take long for the Red and Blacks to score their third goal of the derby. On a counterattack led by Arrascaeta, Samuel Lino finished coolly from the edge of the box to give his side some breathing room. In the second half, Flamengo sat back and let Vasco have the ball, but they rarely troubled goalkeeper Rossi. The Red and Blacks then extended their lead after a brilliant individual run by center-back Léo Ortiz, who surged forward, beat several opponents and struck the crossbar. Samuel Lino side-footed the rebound into the top corner past Léo Jardim to round off the scoring in the derby. 🚦 Where things stand With their fourth straight Brasileirão win, Flamengo reached 73 points and remained clear at the top. The Red and Blacks have a "two-match cushion" over Palmeiras: besides being three points ahead, they have 22 wins to the São Paulo side's 20. Vasco, meanwhile, remained in 13th place with 38 points—four more than Grêmio, who occupy the first relegation spot. Vasco are back in action this Sunday (1), when they face Palmeiras at Nubank Parque in the first leg of the Copa do Brasil semifinals. Flamengo do not play again until Wednesday (4), when they host Grêmio at the Maracanã in Matchday 34 of the Brasileirão. On the same day, Vasco visit Athletico-PR at the Arena da Baixada. item.title: Packers Roster: Which kickers could replace Trey Smack?
item.description: (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images I didn’t think I was going to have to post this midway through a game, but after Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack missed his first extra point after missing two chip shots last week, it seems pretty clear that it’s a question of when — not if — Smack will be replaced. Going into this game, I had done some research on who is available, so I want to share that with you folks. I looked at all kickers who even attempted a field goal from 2024 to 2026, the last three seasons. Outside of punters, there are a total of 55 players who have attempted kicks. Of those 55 players, 46 of them are under contract for other teams or appear to be out of the league entirely, either due to injury or retirement. As far as players on the street go, here’s the list that the Packers can look at during their “mini-bye.” Generally, kickers are worked out before they’re signed, not poached off a practice squad, so I’m not going to include the practice squadders in this list. The Milwaukee Brewers knew when they acquired Dustin May from the St. Louis Cardinals in a trade during the season that there was a chance he’d end up being a half-season rental. The final year of his contract featured a mutual option for 2027. Sure enough, May has declined the option and will become a free agent, Jon Heyman of the New York Post reports. The decision comes just one day after Milwaukee’s World Series win. May’s 5.73 2026 postseason ERA was not ideal, but he did provide depth on the pitching staff. The veteran recorded some big innings in the playoffs and World Series for the Brewers. Overall, May finished the 2026 regular season with a 4.70 ERA across 31 total starts with the Cardinals and Brewers. After beginning his career with the Los Angeles Dodgers back in 2019, May has pitched for four total teams since 2025. He began 2025 with the Dodgers before ending up with the Boston Red Sox, and, as mentioned, he spent 2026 with St. Louis and Milwaukee. If May performs well in 2027 on a one-year contract, he could land a lucrative, multi-year deal next offseason. It remains to be seen if the Brewers will attempt to re-sign the right-handed hurler. item.title: Happy Halloween: Canelo Álvarez Moves Fight Time Due to Holiday
item.description: What to Know No bombs dropped inside or outside at the final pre-fight news conference for the “Mexico vs the World” card in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. All of the card’s fighters appeared on stage, including Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli, along with their teams. The reason for the unexpected early start time: Halloween and Día de los Muertos. The 18 fighters appearing on the “Mexico vs the World” card had their last say in Riyadh on Thursday at the final pre-fight news conference. Despite the concerns swirling around them about the safety of staging the card in a region of the Middle East under attack by Houthi rebels firing missiles and flying explosive-laden drones, everyone appeared relaxed and in good spirits. It’s a bit of a stretch to call it a news conference, given the normal expectation that speakers be asked questions by members of the news media. All questions were scripted and asked by event emcee Richard Schaefer, the 64-year-old former Golden Boy Promotions CEO who now happens to be Canelo’s manager and the executive at the head of Canelo Promotions. An audience appeared to be composed of Saudi officials, royalty, and their guests, who politely applauded during the proceedings. This is an ongoing gripe of ours. If promoters want to stage the scripted presentations, that is their prerogative. But please, don’t insult us by calling them news conferences. Now, we’ll move on. Where’s The Fire? For our taste, the event was far TOO relaxed. Despite coming in as the challenger for the first time in 11 years, Álvarez didn’t demonstrate the kind of passion and fire fans have grown used to seeing from him. item.description: Watch: 'I made the wrong decision,' Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk tells BBC An Australian athlete has admitted putting others at risk by continuing to race after soiling herself during an endurance sports event. Speaking exclusively to the BBC ahead of her return to the sport, Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win the Hyrox race in Beijing in September had clouded her judgement: "It was my decision to continue racing so I take full responsibility for that." Challenged over why she carried on, she said: "I didn't really think about those around me… the decision that I made in hindsight was the wrong decision and I'm truly sorry for everyone that I did affect." The 24-year-old said that the experience and subsequent backlash was "traumatic". She also said she had considered walking away from the sport, in which she holds a world record. Hyrox sees participants alternate between running a kilometre and doing fitness exercises, including a sled push, burpee jumps, indoor rowing, and lunges while carrying a sandbag. The competition has exploded in popularity since it was founded in 2017 in Hamburg, in northern Germany, and is now held across the world. Wietrzyk said she had suffered a bacterial infection from food poisoning [Getty Images] Roughly halfway through her event last month, Wietrzyk suffered a bout of diarrhoea. Images of faecal matter on parts of her body were then shared widely online. Asked whether officials should have stopped her, she said no-one encouraged her to do so the time. Hyrox's co-founder, Moritz Fürste, has issued an apology saying it had been a mistake not to react immediately during the race. New rules have now been introduced giving race directors the power to remove athletes if their vomit, urine or faeces pose a risk of contamination or threaten the welfare of themselves or others in a race that is primarily held indoors using shared equipment. Although initially defiant in a now-deleted Instagram post, Wietrzyk apologised in the week after the Beijing event and said she would forfeit the win and retroactively withdraw from the race. Due to compete in Hamburg on Friday, she said she was "nervous" about her return and hoped that the high-profile incident would not define her. "I don't want it to become my identity," she said. item.title: Pirates Breakout Rookie Feels Healthy After End of Season Injury
item.description: One of the biggest storylines when looking back on the Pittsburgh Pirates ’ 2026 season was the surprise breakout from rookie outfielder Esmerlyn Valdez. The 22-year-old started the season as a promising prospect in Pittsburgh’s farm system, but is now considered to be one of the staples of the team moving forward. Unfortunately, Valdez’s season didn’t end on a high note. He felt something in his leg during a game against the Chicago Cubs in the middle of September and was added to the injured list the next day , ending his season prematurely. The good news is that Valdez doesn’t expect this injury to affect his offseason goals or work. MLB.com’s Jason Mackey recently reported that the rookie resumed baseball activities down at Pittsburgh’s performance camp in Florida. Valdez said he feels great, including running the bases and hitting. This is a great sign for Valdez and the Pirates, since the offseason just got underway with the World Series ending Wednesday night. "I've been running, hitting normally and catching the ball in the outfield. Everything has been good," Valdez said . Sep 9, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Pittsburgh Pirates right fielder Esmerlyn Valdez (55) hits a solo home run during the fifth inning against the Chicago White Sox at Rate Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Now, Valdez can focus on improving his game and preparing for the 2027 season rather than rehabbing what could have been a serious injury. One way Valdez will test his hamstring's stability and improve his game is by participating in the Dominican Winter League. Valdez’s final numbers for the 2026 season were more than impressive. He appeared in 72 games for the Pirates and ended with a .855 OPS, including 17 home runs and 14 doubles. The power in the right-handed hitter is real. Valdez logged an average exit velocity of 92 mph, a barrel rate of 19.9 percent, and a hard-hit rate of 49 percent, all of which ranked well above league average. However, Valdez did have a tendency to punch out, with a strikeout rate of 37.6 percent and a whiff rate of 40.2 percent. This is something the Pirates will definitely want Valdez to work on as long as he’s competing in live game action down in the Dominican Republic this offseason. As long as Valdez is healthy this winter, he’s setting himself up to have a big 2027 season and something that Pittsburgh can look forward to for years to come. The Pirates must make this move to retain arguably the best bat in their lineup for the 2026 season.

He ended with a game-high 28 points on 11-for-17 shooting to match six rebounds, four assists, and five stocks. item.description: North Dakota State's stadium future is something to watch for the coming years. Getty North Dakota State has enjoyed a mostly successful first year in the FBS, starting 6-2, but a Bison insider sees a glaring need. The Fargo Forum’s Mike McFeely couldn’t ignore the home stadium of NDSU’s most recent opponent in New Mexico and how the state is paying for major upgrades. McFeely recently sounded off on how he believes the North Dakota state legislature needs to do the same for the Bison amid an 18,000-seat Fargodome that opened in 1992 and can’t easily expand seating. “Like New Mexico, NDSU plays in a stadium that famously needs improvements,” McFeely wrote. “The 34-year-old Fargodome needs many of the same renovations that University Stadium will get, yet nobody can quite figure out how to pay for them.” “There’s also some chatter that NDSU might be interested in building its own stadium, so it doesn’t have to deal with the city of Fargo government [which owns the dome] and the Fargo Dome Authority [which manages it],” McFeely added. He went on to explore the costs and what both New Mexico and Hawaii have done for similar stadium projects in the Mountain West Conference . His column can be read here . Until the day arrives for the Bison to have a new stadium, the program has a fierce home-field advantage, with a 206-29 home record through the Division II and FCS eras. That hasn’t changed in the FBS with a 4-0 home record thus far.
